Solve the following multiple-choice mathematics problem. You may reason before answering. End your final response with exactly "ANSWER: X", where X is one of A, B, C, D, E. Select one option.

how many seconds will a 650 meter long train moving with a speed of 63 km / hr take to cross a man walking with a speed of 3 km / hr in the direction of the train ?

A. 48
B. 36
C. 26
D. 39
E. 18

message.content:
Relative speed 60 km/h = 50/3 m/s; 650/(50/3)=39. D</think>Relative speed = 63 − 3 = 60 km/hr = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s.

Time = 650 ÷ (50/3) = 650 × 3/50 = 39 seconds.

ANSWER: D

final_content:
Relative speed = 63 − 3 = 60 km/hr = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s.

Time = 650 ÷ (50/3) = 650 × 3/50 = 39 seconds.

ANSWER: D
